subject: Stanfit object from in progress sample file

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Stanfit object from in progress sample file
parts:
Hi folks, 

I'm running a very long chain (in R) for which I specified a sample file so I could check its progress as it goes. Has anyone written code to convert a partially completed sample file to a stanfit object so that all the standard summaries and diagnostics can be run? I'll try my hand at this if not, but thought I should check before reinventing the wheel.

Oh, and I should also double-check my understanding of how the sampling works (and the reasonability of monitoring progress in this manner) by asking: there's no difference in what the sampler is doing between the "warm up" and  "sampling" phases, right? The division of these phases only affects what gets tossed before the summaries and diagnostics are run, correct?


--

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Stanfit object from in progress sample file
parts:
There is a read_stan_csv() function in RStan that is supposed to work in this situation. The warm up phase is conceptually different from the sampling stage, which is why we don't call it burnin. There is a lot of adaptation going on during the warm up phase in HMC.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Stanfit object from in progress sample file
parts:
The Stan manual has a section on the algorithms used
during warmup.

The key thing is that the warmup iterations aren't proper
draws from the posterior and so must be discarded for inference.

- Bob
